text.p: A young woman who drowned after falling down a cliff-face blowhole on Thursday was the daughter of a woman killed when seven people were sucked down the same blowhole five years ago, Australian police said on Friday.
Two young women, aged 16 and 20, died on Thursday after falling down the blowhole south of Sydney and being sucked out into the Pacific Ocean.

"We believe they are (related)," a police spokesman told Reuters. "From what we can gather through our inquiries, it was the younger one, the 16-year-old -- her mother died in the blowhole five years ago."
Seven people died in 1992 when two families were sucked into the ocean by a freak wave surging through the same blowhole at Kiama, a fishing village 120 km (80 miles) south of Sydney.
A post mortem examination of the two bodies was to be held on Friday and a coronial inquest established at a later date.
Surviving family members had asked for the names of both women not to be released, the spokesman said.
Police refused to speculate on whether the two latest deaths could have been suicide, saying circumstances surrounding the tragedy would be decided by the state coroner.
More than 300,000 visitors each year flock to the blowhole.
Blowholes are weathered openings in cliff faces where ocean waves rush in and cause spectacular explosions of white water resulting in volcano-like gushes.
Teenagers have been known to leap into the Kiama blowhole for a daring and terrifying swim to safety.
